modules.title: Supply Chain Management
modules.description: Supply chain fundamentals and end-to-end coordination

modules.title: Demand Planning
modules.description: Understand customer and market demand and develop the demand perspective that supports S&OP planning.

modules.title: Supply Planning
modules.description: Understand how organizations translate demand plans into feasible supply plans by coordinating production, procurement, inventory, capacity, workforce, suppliers, and fulfillment.

modules.title: Inventory Management
modules.description: Understand inventory fundamentals, inventory types, inventory planning and control, replenishment, availability, costs, and working-capital trade-offs in manufacturing and S&OP.

modules.title: Demand-Supply Reconciliation
modules.description: Compare demand requirements with available and planned supply, identify imbalances across products and time periods, and develop coordinated S&OP responses.

modules.title: S&OP Governance and Management
modules.description: S&OP governance, cross-functional roles, management reviews, approved plans, implementation, and execution alignment.

modules.title: S&OP Performance Measurement and KPIs
modules.description: Measure and interpret performance across demand, supply, inventory, customer service, financial results, and the S&OP process.

topics.title: What is Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP)?
topics.summary: Understand what S&OP is, why companies need it, what business problems it solves, and how it connects departments.

topics.title: Purpose and Benefits of Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP)
topics.summary: Understand why companies implement S&OP, the business problems it addresses, its operational and financial benefits, and how it supports cross-functional decisions.

topics.title: Understanding Demand and Supply
topics.summary: Understand demand and supply in business and manufacturing, distinguish customer needs, orders, actual sales and forecasted demand, assess supply capability and constraints, and analyze demand-supply gaps in S&OP.

topics.title: Departments Involved in Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP)
topics.summary: Understand why S&OP requires cross-functional collaboration, the responsibilities and information contributions of Sales, Demand Planning, Manufacturing, Procurement, Supply Planning, Inventory, Finance, Product Management and Executive Leadership, how departments interact, how S&OP resolves conflicts, and how an S&OP Analyst supports aligned business decisions.

topics.title: S&OP vs. Other Planning Processes
topics.summary: Understand how S&OP differs from strategic, tactical, and operational planning; distinguish Demand Planning, Supply Planning, MPS, MRP, Production Scheduling, S&OE, and financial planning; and explain how the processes connect business objectives with manufacturing execution.

topics.title: Planning Horizons in Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP)
topics.summary: Understand short-term, medium-term, and long-term planning; distinguish planning horizon, frequency, and bucket; and connect rolling S&OP plans with strategic direction and operational execution.

topics.title: Introduction to Financial Planning
topics.summary: Understand how financial planning connects with operational planning in S&OP, including revenue, costs, profitability, financial statements, working capital, cash flow, and the financial implications of manufacturing and inventory decisions.

topics.title: What is Supply Chain Management (SCM)?
topics.summary: Understand what a supply chain is, how Supply Chain Management coordinates suppliers, manufacturers, distributors, and customers, the material, information, and financial flows, supply chain objectives and trade-offs, and how S&OP supports end-to-end supply chain coordination.

topics.title: Supply Chain Components
topics.summary: Understand the major components of a supply chain, their individual responsibilities, how they interact, and how suppliers, procurement, manufacturing, inventory, logistics, distribution, customers, and supporting functions influence S&OP.

topics.title: Understanding Product Flow in Supply Chain Management
topics.summary: Understand the end-to-end physical movement of materials and products from suppliers to customers, the inbound, internal, and outbound stages, inventory transformation and availability, production bottlenecks, supply chain disruptions, and how product flow information supports S&OP decisions.

topics.title: Understanding Demand Information
topics.summary: Understand the sources and types of demand information, distinguish actual demand, sales, customer orders, backlog and forecasts, classify demand by time, product, customer and value, recognize demand patterns and data-quality problems, evaluate demand adjustments and exceptions, consolidate demand without double-counting, and explain how reliable demand information supports S&OP.

topics.title: Product Classification and Product Families
topics.summary: Understand product classification and product hierarchies, distinguish product portfolios, categories, families, groups, models and SKUs, define product families for different planning purposes, aggregate SKU-level demand, recognize aggregation risks, and apply product-family analysis to manufacturing and S&OP decisions.

topics.title: Manufacturing Strategies
topics.summary: Understand Make-to-Stock (MTS), Make-to-Order (MTO), Assemble-to-Order (ATO), and Engineer-to-Order (ETO); compare their production triggers, inventory requirements, customization, lead times, forecasting and capacity needs; explain push, pull, decoupling points, CODP and postponement; evaluate strategy selection factors; and apply manufacturing strategies to demand, supply, capacity, procurement, inventory, financial planning, and S&OP decisions.

topics.title: Introduction to Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)
topics.summary: Understand KPI fundamentals and the differences between measurements, metrics, KPIs, targets, actual results, and variances; distinguish leading and lagging indicators; select effective SMART-aligned KPIs; understand demand, supply, inventory, customer service, financial, and S&OP process KPI categories; evaluate targets and performance trade-offs; and use manufacturing KPI scorecards to support S&OP decisions and continuous improvement.

topics.title: Demand Planning KPIs
topics.summary: Understand how organizations measure demand planning performance, evaluate forecast quality, accuracy and bias, calculate and interpret MAPE, WAPE, MAE, Forecast Bias, FVA and Forecast Attainment, identify product-level and aggregate forecasting problems, and use demand KPIs to improve S&OP decisions.

topics.title: Supply Planning KPIs
topics.summary: Understand how manufacturing organizations measure production plan attainment, schedule adherence, capacity utilization, OEE, production yield, customer and supplier on-time delivery, supplier lead time performance, and supply plan attainment; calculate and interpret supply performance, identify production and material constraints, and use supply KPIs to assess S&OP plan feasibility and support operational and management decisions.

topics.title: Inventory KPIs
topics.summary: Understand how manufacturing organizations measure inventory performance, calculate inventory turnover, days of inventory and supply, average inventory, inventory accuracy, stockout rate, fill rate, service level, excess and obsolete inventory, and carrying cost; analyze raw materials, WIP and finished goods; identify shortages and excess stocks; and use inventory KPIs to support S&OP decisions and evaluate working-capital implications.

topics.title: Financial KPIs
topics.summary: Understand how manufacturing organizations measure financial performance in S&OP, calculate revenue, COGS, gross and operating profit, margins, production cost, inventory carrying cost, working capital, inventory value, budget variance, and forecast-versus-actual performance, and evaluate the financial impact of demand, supply, production, procurement, and inventory decisions.

topics.title: KPI Analysis and Interpretation
topics.summary: Understand how to analyze and interpret S&OP KPIs, calculate and investigate performance variances and trends, identify relationships and trade-offs between demand, supply, inventory, and financial indicators, apply root cause analysis and segmentation, and translate validated findings into actionable management recommendations.

topics.title: Data Analytics for S&OP
topics.summary: Understand how to prepare and analyze S&OP data, apply descriptive, diagnostic, predictive, and prescriptive analytics, investigate demand, supply, inventory, and supplier performance, use Excel, Power BI, SQL, and Python, and translate analytical findings into actionable business recommendations.

topics.title: S&OP Reporting and Dashboard
topics.summary: Understand how S&OP reports and dashboards communicate business performance, monitor demand, supply, inventory, capacity, and financial KPIs, identify exceptions, validate and consolidate data, use Excel, Power BI, SQL, and Python for reporting, and translate findings into management decisions.

topics.title: Continuous Improvement
topics.summary: Understand how to improve S&OP through KPI monitoring, performance gap analysis, root cause investigation, PDCA, DMAIC, Kaizen, Lean, Six Sigma, measurable improvement initiatives, action ownership, effectiveness measurement, and sustainable process controls.

topics.title: S&OP Outputs and Implementation
topics.summary: Understand the planning outputs and management decisions generated by S&OP, how approved plans are communicated and translated into departmental actions, how ownership and version control maintain alignment, and how execution is monitored through action tracking, actual-versus-plan analysis, corrective actions, and escalation.

topics.title: S&OP vs. S&OE
topics.summary: Understand the differences between Sales & Operations Planning and Sales & Operations Execution, their planning horizons, responsibilities, processes, KPIs, escalation rules, feedback loop, and how an S&OP Analyst connects medium-term planning with short-term manufacturing execution.

topics.title: Roles and Responsibilities
topics.summary: Understand the cross-functional S&OP organizational structure, departmental roles, responsibilities throughout the S&OP cycle, decision authority, accountability, collaboration, escalation, the S&OP Analyst's role, and how to apply a RACI Matrix in a manufacturing environment.

topics.title: Executive S&OP Meeting
topics.summary: Understand the purpose and position of the Executive S&OP Meeting, executive participants and decision rights, meeting inputs and activities, exception-based management, strategic demand-supply-financial trade-offs, approved plan outputs, and the S&OP Analyst's role in executive reporting, recommendations, decision records, and action monitoring.

topics.title: Understanding Planning Data
topics.summary: Understand planning data and distinguish master, transactional, historical, planning, and reference data; identify demand, supply, and inventory inputs; organize data by time, product, location, and business dimensions; understand ERP, MES, MRP, WMS, CRM, and other data sources; validate, cleanse, reconcile, and prepare planning datasets; distinguish actual records from assumptions and parameters; and assess data reliability for S&OP decisions.

topics.title: Understanding Demand
topics.summary: Understand what demand represents in business and supply chain planning; distinguish customer needs, actual demand, sales, customer orders, open orders, backlog, historical demand, and forecasted demand; classify independent, dependent, derived, unconstrained, and constrained demand; identify internal and external demand drivers, demand patterns, planning levels, variability, and uncertainty; and apply demand analysis to manufacturing and S&OP decisions.

topics.title: Types of Demand Information
topics.summary: Understand historical demand and actual sales, customer orders and backlog, customer forecasts, internal Sales input, statistical forecasts, market intelligence, promotional and new-product demand, and documented demand adjustments; evaluate source reliability, consolidate overlapping information without double-counting, and prepare a validated demand planning input for S&OP.

topics.title: Introduction to Demand Forecasting
topics.summary: Understand demand forecasting and its role in S&OP; distinguish forecasts from customer orders, sales forecasts, targets, budgets, demand plans, supply plans and production plans; evaluate historical, customer, commercial, product and external forecasting inputs; compare qualitative and quantitative approaches; understand forecast levels, granularity, aggregation, horizons, the forecasting workflow and uncertainty; and apply demand forecasting concepts to manufacturing and cross-functional planning decisions.

topics.title: Quantitative Forecasting Methods
topics.summary: Understand and apply quantitative forecasting methods using historical demand data; calculate and compare naive forecasts, simple and weighted moving averages, simple exponential smoothing, linear trend regression, and basic seasonal forecasts; evaluate forecast errors using MAD, MAPE, MSE and bias; select methods based on demand patterns; and interpret statistical forecasts for manufacturing, procurement, inventory, and S&OP Demand Review decisions.

topics.title: Demand Influencing Factors
topics.summary: Understand internal business, external market, product, and customer-related factors that influence demand; distinguish normal variation, event-driven changes, temporary changes, structural changes, incremental demand, and demand shifts; quantify forecast adjustments, avoid double-counting, and evaluate demand assumptions and risks during S&OP Demand Review.

topics.title: Consensus Demand Planning
topics.summary: Understand how statistical forecasts, customer information, market intelligence, and cross-functional inputs are evaluated and reconciled into one agreed demand plan; assess judgmental adjustments, avoid double-counting, conduct Demand Reviews, resolve conflicting assumptions, and communicate demand risks and decisions in S&OP.

topics.title: Forecast Accuracy and Forecast Bias
topics.summary: Understand how to measure forecast accuracy and error using MAD, MAPE, WAPE, MSE and RMSE; measure cumulative forecast error, mean forecast error and forecast bias; interpret forecasting performance at SKU, product-family and aggregate levels; investigate root causes; and use forecast KPIs to improve manufacturing and S&OP Demand Reviews.

topics.title: Understanding Supply Planning
topics.summary: Understand what Supply Planning is, how it differs from Demand Planning, what makes a supply plan feasible, the objectives and components of supply planning, required planning information, the supply planning process and strategies, and how S&OP analysts identify constraints, evaluate supply alternatives, and communicate supply gaps.

topics.title: Production Planning Fundamentals
topics.summary: Understand production planning objectives, inputs, production strategies, planning steps, gross and net production requirements, lot size, production rate, lead time, yield, scrap, inventory and WIP; calculate production quantities and projected ending inventory; evaluate material and capacity feasibility; and apply production planning analysis to S&OP Supply Review decisions.

topics.title: Capacity Planning
topics.summary: Understand capacity planning and its role in Supply Planning and S&OP; distinguish design capacity, effective capacity, actual output, and practical available capacity; calculate available and required production capacity, utilization, efficiency, capacity gap, and capacity cushion; evaluate machine rates, shifts, downtime, setup, labor, and yield; apply Rough-Cut Capacity Planning (RCCP); and assess capacity-management options such as overtime, additional shifts, subcontracting, rescheduling, inventory build-ahead, and capacity investment.

topics.title: Resource Planning
topics.summary: Understand resource planning and its role in Supply Planning and S&OP; distinguish resource, capacity, and production planning; identify manpower, machines, materials, tools, utilities, and time requirements; calculate labor-hours, machine-hours, material needs, availability, utilization, and resource gaps; evaluate resource constraints, allocation, shortages, surpluses, and corrective actions; and apply resource feasibility analysis to manufacturing and cross-functional S&OP decisions.

topics.title: Lead Time Management
topics.summary: Understand lead time and its role in supply chain planning; distinguish procurement, manufacturing, order processing, transportation, cumulative, and end-to-end lead times; measure planned and actual lead time, average duration, variability, and reliability; calculate cumulative lead time and estimated completion and delivery dates using calendar and working days; analyze the effects of lead time on procurement, production, inventory, customer service, and S&OP planning; and evaluate strategies to improve lead time and manage supplier delays.

topics.title: Bottleneck Analysis
topics.summary: Understand how to identify, measure, analyze, and manage production bottlenecks; distinguish bottlenecks, constraints, and capacity shortages; calculate process capacity, throughput, cycle time, utilization, and capacity gaps; apply the Theory of Constraints and its Five Focusing Steps; evaluate bottleneck improvement alternatives; and communicate capacity constraints and their business implications during S&OP Supply Review and Pre-S&OP.

topics.title: Supply Planning Strategies
topics.summary: Understand supply planning strategy selection; compare Make-to-Stock, Make-to-Order, Assemble-to-Order, level, chase, hybrid, inventory build-ahead and production smoothing; evaluate overtime, subcontracting, alternative lines, rescheduling, allocation and supplier flexibility; calculate production requirements, inventory projections, capacity utilization and supply-demand gaps; compare supply alternatives and communicate recommendations during Supply Review and Pre-S&OP.

topics.title: Feasible Supply Plan
topics.summary: Understand how to develop, validate, and evaluate a feasible supply plan by integrating demand requirements, production capacity, manpower, materials, inventory, supplier capabilities, lead times, bottlenecks, and operational constraints; calculate production requirements, available supply, projected inventory, supply-demand gaps, capacity feasibility, material shortages, and backlog; compare alternative supply scenarios; and communicate data-supported recommendations during Supply Review and Pre-S&OP.

topics.title: Understanding Inventory
topics.summary: Understand inventory fundamentals and its role in manufacturing, supply chain operations, and S&OP; distinguish inventory, stock, and available supply; explain inventory functions, supply chain flow, inventory costs, working-capital implications, understocking and overstocking, raw materials, WIP and finished goods, the inventory balance equation, and inventory-related S&OP decisions.

topics.title: Types of Inventory
topics.summary: Understand inventory classification by production stage, function or purpose, and demand characteristics; distinguish raw materials, work-in-process, finished goods, MRO, cycle stock, safety stock, pipeline, anticipation and decoupling inventory; explain independent and dependent demand; trace inventory movement through manufacturing; and apply inventory classification to supply planning and S&OP decisions.

topics.title: Demand-Supply Matching
topics.summary: Understand how organizations compare customer orders and forecasts against available inventory, planned production, scheduled receipts, procurement, materials, and capacity; calculate available supply, supply-demand gaps, projected inventory, unfulfilled demand, backlog, and cumulative balances; analyze multi-product, multi-period manufacturing scenarios; distinguish temporary timing gaps from structural shortages; and communicate demand-supply mismatches to support S&OP decisions.

topics.title: Understanding the S&OP Cycle
topics.summary: Understand the complete recurring S&OP cycle, its five stages, activities, participants, inputs and outputs; trace demand, supply and financial information through the process; understand monthly calendars, cross-functional collaboration, one agreed set of numbers, governance, escalation, executive decisions, implementation, and the feedback loop.

topics.title: Inventory Position
topics.summary: Understand how to determine inventory position by combining usable on-hand stock, qualified incoming purchase and production supply, reservations, customer and production commitments, and outstanding demand; distinguish on-hand, available inventory, inventory position, ATP, and PAB; calculate inventory position, available inventory, projected balances, multi-period positions, and net requirements; and apply timing-aware inventory analysis to manufacturing and S&OP decisions.

topics.title: Average Daily Usage (ADU)
topics.summary: Understand Average Daily Usage and how to calculate historical, working-day, calendar-day, simple and weighted consumption rates; select appropriate usage data for raw materials, WIP and finished goods; analyze demand, production volume, product mix, yield, scrap and unusual consumption; project material usage; and apply ADU to inventory coverage, replenishment, and S&OP decisions.

topics.title: Days of Supply (DOS)
topics.summary: Understand Days of Supply and how to calculate and interpret inventory coverage using on-hand, available inventory, and inventory position; distinguish calendar-day and working-day coverage; evaluate consumption changes, receipts, allocations, variability and lead times; project inventory depletion and stockout timing; calculate target inventory and coverage gaps; and apply DOS to manufacturing, procurement, production planning, and S&OP decisions.

topics.title: Lead Time and Safety Stock
topics.summary: Understand procurement, production, and replenishment lead time; distinguish planned and actual lead time; explain safety stock, cycle stock, and excess inventory; analyze demand and lead time variability, supplier reliability, forecast accuracy, and service levels; calculate safety stock using buffer days, demand variability, lead time variability, and combined variability; and apply inventory protection calculations to manufacturing and S&OP decisions.

topics.title: Reorder Point (ROP)
topics.summary: Understand how Reorder Point determines when to replenish inventory; calculate ROP using average daily usage, replenishment lead time, and safety stock; account for variable demand and lead time, inventory position, open purchase orders, allocations and backorders; calculate replenishment quantities; and apply ROP monitoring to manufacturing procurement, production planning, and S&OP decisions.

topics.title: Inventory Turnover
topics.summary: Understand inventory turnover and its relationship to average inventory, COGS, DOS and DIO; calculate monthly, quarterly, annual and annualized turnover using consistent valuation bases; analyze value-based and quantity-based turnover; compare raw materials, WIP and finished goods; identify slow-moving and fast-moving inventory; and apply turnover analysis to demand, supply, procurement, production, working-capital and S&OP decisions.

topics.title: ABC Classification
topics.summary: Understand ABC Classification and the Pareto Principle; calculate annual consumption value, value percentages and cumulative percentages; rank and classify inventory into A, B and C categories; apply differentiated inventory controls; recognize operational-criticality limitations; and use ABC results with inventory turnover and S&OP decisions.

topics.title: XYZ Classification
topics.summary: Understand XYZ Classification and demand variability; calculate mean, standard deviation and coefficient of variation; classify inventory into X, Y and Z categories; interpret regular and intermittent consumption; apply demand predictability to forecasting, safety stock and replenishment; combine ABC-XYZ classification; and use variability analysis to support inventory and S&OP decisions.

topics.title: Excess and Obsolete Inventory
topics.summary: Understand how to identify, measure, manage, and prevent excess, slow-moving, non-moving, and obsolete inventory; compare inventory position and projected requirements with target inventory and future demand; calculate excess quantity and value, inventory aging and coverage, slow-moving inventory percentage, obsolete inventory value, and potential inventory reduction; assess write-downs, write-offs, working-capital exposure, and manufacturing scenarios involving raw materials, WIP, finished goods, demand changes, engineering revisions, and discontinued products; and coordinate recovery, prevention, and management decisions across Sales, Operations, Procurement, Engineering, Finance, and S&OP.

topics.title: Identifying Supply Gaps
topics.summary: Understand how to identify, measure, investigate, and analyze supply gaps across products and time periods; distinguish supply, capacity, material and delivery shortages; calculate gross and net gaps, projected inventory shortfalls, cumulative gaps, demand fulfillment and backlog; apply Pareto Analysis and the 5 Whys; and communicate operational and financial impacts during Supply Review and Pre-S&OP.

topics.title: Supply-Demand Balancing Strategies
topics.summary: Understand how companies develop and evaluate supply-side and demand-side strategies to balance customer demand with available supply; compare overtime, additional shifts, subcontracting, alternative production lines, material expediting, inventory reallocation, build-ahead, demand rescheduling, allocation and product substitution; apply level and chase production, inventory drawdown, backlog and excess-supply analysis; calculate supply-demand gaps, additional production and capacity, inventory impact, remaining backlog, incremental balancing costs and demand fulfillment; evaluate operational feasibility, cost, customer service, revenue, profitability and multi-period impacts; and present cross-functional balancing recommendations during Supply Review and Pre-S&OP.

topics.title: Demand Prioritization
topics.summary: Understand how companies prioritize customer demand when available supply, production capacity, or inventory is insufficient; evaluate customer importance, delivery urgency, revenue, contribution, contractual obligations, product criticality and business impact; compare FIFO, customer-based, proportional, priority-based, product/market-based and fair-share allocation; calculate available supply, allocations, remaining supply, unfulfilled demand, backlog, fulfillment rates, revenue and contribution impact; apply alternative allocation approaches to a manufacturing scenario; and develop cross-functional, data-supported S&OP allocation recommendations.

topics.title: Scenario Planning
topics.summary: Understand how companies develop, evaluate, and compare alternative business scenarios involving demand, supply, capacity, inventory, supplier disruptions, and financial conditions; distinguish forecasting, scenario planning, sensitivity analysis, and contingency planning; calculate scenario demand, feasible production, available supply, projected inventory, supply-demand gaps, capacity utilization, fulfillment, revenue, costs, profitability, risk exposure, and expected outcomes; develop base, upside, downside, and combined manufacturing scenarios; identify trigger points and contingency actions; and prepare scenario analysis and recommendations for Pre-S&OP and management review.
